**Summary**

I researched Apple's most recent reported results — the fiscal 2024 fourth quarter (ended September 28, 2024) reported October 31, 2024 — and confirmed the figures against Apple's Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR. Apple posted quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year in the iPhone 16 launch quarter, and full-year FY2024 net sales of $391.0 billion (up from $383.3 billion in FY2023) with net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08, both depressed by a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge tied to the European State Aid decision; operating income was $123.2 billion. Read through the tax charge, underlying earnings power is meaningfully higher, revenue is re-accelerating, and the setup into the December quarter is supported by the iPhone 16 cycle and the phased Apple Intelligence rollout — a combination I judged favourable enough to add exposure despite a rich multiple (about 36x reported FY2024 EPS at ~$222.70). I checked the live quote ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask) and placed a single limit buy order for 40 shares of AAPL at $223.00, which filled at $223.00 for a total of $8,920 — comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order cap, the only trade today (so well under the $20,000 daily total), a limit price within ~0.15% of the market, and no money moved out of the account (cash now ~$41,080, alongside the existing 100 MSFT shares).
